reasons.title: prefix_binding_mismatch: thinking dropped because the conversation before it changed
reasons.meaning: Something before this thinking block (system, tools or an earlier message) changed after Claude produced it, so the API dropped the block. That happens with `prefix_mismatch_behavior: "drop_block"`.

sources.quote: `thinking_dropped`, `prefix_binding_mismatch`: What came before this block isn’t what it recorded. Yours to fix

faq.q: Does prefix_binding_mismatch cost me anything?
faq.a: You aren't billed for the dropped block, but Claude can spend more output tokens working out reasoning it can no longer read, and dropping it invalidates the prompt cache from the first dropped block onward. When something changes on every turn, the increase repeats.

faq.q: How do I find what changed?
faq.a: Compare `system`, `tools` and `messages` up to the first entry's `path` with the conversation as it was when that block was produced. If every block is listed, start with `system` and `tools`. Or paste both requests into the prefix checker above.

faq.q: Should my tests fail on this entry?
faq.a: Yes. Anthropic's test steps say to fail only on an entry whose reason is `prefix_binding_mismatch`; model and organization entries are expected after a switch.

reasons.title: thinking_mismatch_allowed: Claude read stale thinking and you were billed for it
reasons.meaning: The thinking block failed the prefix check, but with the setting unset this model let it through: Claude read it unchanged and you were billed for it. It's reasoning about content that has since changed.

sources.quote: `thinking_mismatch_allowed`, `prefix_binding_mismatch`: The same, but Claude read the block unchanged, and it’s billed. This entry appears only where the setting is unset, on some models. Yours to fix.
When no error is returned, the failing blocks reach the model. Claude reads them like any other input, you’re billed for them, and Claude works from reasoning about content that has since changed.

faq.q: Why didn't I get a 400 error?
faq.a: On Claude Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5, a request that fails the prefix check with the setting unset might get a 400 or no error. With no error, the failing blocks reach Claude and are billed. Send `prefix_mismatch_behavior: "error"` in tests so every failure is a 400.

faq.q: Does the beta header change what Claude reads?
faq.a: No. Sending `thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01` with the setting unset only adds the `input_transformations` array so you can log these entries.

reasons.title: model_binding_mismatch: this Claude model can't read thinking from the model that produced it
reasons.meaning: You switched models mid-conversation and the new model can't read the old model's thinking. The API drops it for this request only, with no error and no charge.

sources.quote: `thinking_dropped`, `model_binding_mismatch`: This model can’t read blocks from the model that produced it. Not yours to fix

faq.q: Should I remove those blocks?
faq.a: No. Keep sending the whole conversation. If you switch back to a model that can read them, they're read again, because the API never changes your `messages`.

faq.q: Which switches keep the reasoning?
faq.a: See the model-switch tab: for example, Claude Fable 5.2 reads blocks from Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5, but no other model reads Fable 5.2's blocks.

reasons.title: organization_binding_mismatch: thinking from another account was dropped
reasons.meaning: The thinking block came from a different account (organization, AWS account or Google Cloud project), so the API dropped it.

sources.quote: `thinking_dropped`, `organization_binding_mismatch`: Another account produced the block, so the API dropped it. Not yours to fix.
Thinking blocks from Claude Fable 5.2, Claude Mythos 5.2, Claude Sonnet 5.5, and Claude Haiku 5.5 work only in the account that produced them or a linked one.

faq.q: What counts as my account?
faq.a: On the Claude API, Claude Platform on AWS, Anthropic-managed Google Cloud and Microsoft Foundry it's your organization; on Amazon Bedrock it's your AWS account; on Google-managed Google Cloud it's your Google Cloud project.

faq.q: Is this an error?
faq.a: No. The request still succeeds and Claude answers without that block's reasoning.

reasons.title: prefix_mismatch: GPT-6.2 removed reasoning after a prefix edit
reasons.meaning: Content before this reasoning item was inserted or edited, so GPT-6.2 or later removed the item. The request still succeeded.

sources.quote: On GPT-6.2 and later, you insert or edit content before the reasoning item. For example, rewriting an earlier tool result changes the prefix.

Starting with GPT-6.2, the Responses API drops reasoning items after mid-conversation edits to the conversation history (prefix edits), certain model changes (including downgrades), or changes to the end user or organization.

faq.q: Does deleting old items cause prefix_mismatch?
faq.a: Not by itself. OpenAI's reasoning guide says deleting whole items without editing the remaining items, or appending new items after the reasoning item, does not trigger this reason.

faq.q: How do I change reasoning effort or tools without it?
faq.a: Append a `configuration_update` item for effort or format, or an `additional_tools` item for tools, instead of changing the request-level parameters.

reasons.title: end_user_mismatch: safety_identifier differs between requests
reasons.meaning: The request that reused this reasoning item had a different `safety_identifier` from the one that created it (or only one of them had one).

sources.quote: the `safety_identifier` on the request that created the item differs from the one on the request that reuses it, including supplying an identifier on only one of the two requests

faq.q: I only added safety_identifier to new requests. Is that enough to trigger it?
faq.a: Yes. Supplying an identifier on only one of the two requests counts.

reasons.title: model_mismatch: reasoning removed after a model switch
reasons.meaning: You switched to a different model family, or to a less capable model in the same family, so the earlier reasoning items were removed.

sources.quote: You switch model families or move to a less capable model within the same family.
Persisted reasoning can be reused only within the same model family.

faq.q: Does all_turns keep reasoning across model families?
faq.a: No. A different family drops it even when `reasoning.context` is `all_turns`.

faq.q: Which model in a family is more capable?
faq.a: OpenAI doesn't publish an order for astra, sol, terra and luna, so the model-switch tab shows both outcomes for a same-family switch.

reasons.title: organization_mismatch: reasoning item from another organization
reasons.meaning: The reasoning item was created in another organization (or another workspace under a different user), so it was removed.

sources.quote: You reuse an item from another organization, or from a different workspace under a different user.

faq.q: Can I move reasoning items between organizations?
faq.a: No. The item is removed and the request continues without it.

reasons.title: turn_boundary: earlier-turn reasoning not used
reasons.meaning: The model used only current-turn reasoning, so a reasoning item from an earlier turn wasn't used.

sources.quote: The item comes from an earlier turn and the model uses only current-turn reasoning.
The GPT-5.6 model family supports `all_turns` and uses it by default. Earlier models default to `current_turn`. GPT-6.1 Sol also supports `all_turns`.

faq.q: How do I keep reasoning from earlier turns?
faq.a: Set `reasoning.context: "all_turns"` on a model that supports it (the GPT-5.6 family and GPT-6.1 Sol, per OpenAI's reasoning guide). Defaults for GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6.2 aren't stated, so check the response's `reasoning.context` field.

errors.example_message: messages.1.content.0: Invalid `signature` in `thinking` block. The block is bound to a different conversation. Remove the block, or set `thinking.block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior` to "drop_block".
errors.meaning: A thinking block failed the prefix check: `system`, `tools` or an earlier message changed after Claude produced it, or a thinking block between others was left out or moved. "A different conversation" means different content before the block, not a different session or user.

Match only on “The block is bound to a different conversation”, because the rest of the message can change.
Every 400 error has the type `invalid_request_error`, and this one has no `error.details.error_code`.

faq.q: Why doesn't sending the same request again work?
faq.a: Your history still holds what your code changed. Send `"drop_block"` (with the beta header) on every later request in that conversation to stop the errors, then make your code append-only.

faq.q: The error says to remove the block. Is that enough?
faq.a: No. Removing only that block isn't enough: remove it and every `thinking` and `redacted_thinking` block after it, or the same error names the next invalid one.

faq.q: How should my code detect this error?
faq.a: Match only on the phrase "The block is bound to a different conversation". The rest of the message can change, and the error has no `error.details.error_code`.

sources.quote: If the request had no beta header, the error message adds this sentence
If the error still asks for the header, the header didn’t reach the API: a proxy or library might have removed it.

faq.q: How do I send the header with the SDK?
faq.a: Call the beta Messages method and pass `betas=["thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01"]` (Python) or `betas: ["thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01"]` (TypeScript).

faq.q: Can a gateway strip the header but keep the setting?
faq.a: It shouldn't: forwarding the setting without the header gets a 400. Gateways should pass `anthropic-beta` values and `thinking.block_binding` through as sent.
